subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should Doctor classify a runtime-valid, non-loopback trusted-proxy Gateway as configured authentication and emit the guarded proxy/firewall WARNING instead of the current unauthenticated CRITICAL?
rationale: The code can align Doctor with the documented and runtime-enforced trusted-proxy contract, but choosing whether that guarded state should suppress the strongest exposed-bind diagnosis is a security-policy decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Accept guarded trusted-proxy warning
options.body: Merge after rebase if Gateway/security owners agree that runtime-valid trusted-proxy authentication is sufficient for the exposed-bind diagnostic while firewall guidance remains prominent.

options.title: Retain universal CRITICAL
options.body: Keep the existing Doctor severity for every non-loopback trusted-proxy deployment if maintainers want exposure diagnostics to require a shared secret regardless of runtime auth validity.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded trusted-proxy warning
recommendation.body: Merge after rebase if Gateway/security owners agree that runtime-valid trusted-proxy authentication is sufficient for the exposed-bind diagnostic while firewall guidance remains prominent.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway auth history shows sustained ownership of trusted-proxy security behavior and fail-closed auth boundaries.
